title: Trees: structure, answers, and work
description: Build and trace subtree answers, mirror a hierarchy at every level, search for the first matching path, count traversal work, then produce a shipment report.

learned: State what a completed recursive call returns for its own subtree.
Tell structure from labels: a leaf is a node with no children.
Build a new tree from child results without changing the original.
Stop a search at the first match, and count the work a traversal really does.
recap.invariant: Each completed call returns a correct answer for exactly its own subtree.
recap.complexity: Whole-tree aggregation: Θ(n) time and O(h) recursive stack space with constant-time selectors and bounded-size arithmetic; drawing is excluded.
recap.common_mistake: Deciding the base case from a label (such as label == 1 or a falsy label) instead of from an empty child sequence.
in_real_programs: Python ast.iter_child_nodes exposes immediate child nodes for syntax-tree traversal.

retrieval.question: Module 4: what does using selectors protect?
retrieval.answer: Clients depend on the interface instead of the concrete representation.
